_note: Short paraphrased descriptions for the techniques used by the bundled rules. Authoritative definitions: https://attack.mitre.org/. Mappings indicate which behaviour a rule relates to; they are not proof of attacker activity.

T1003.001.name: OS Credential Dumping: LSASS Memory
T1003.001.description: Adversaries may read credential material from the memory of the LSASS process.

T1021.001.name: Remote Services: Remote Desktop Protocol
T1021.001.description: Adversaries may use valid accounts to log in to remote systems over RDP.

T1021.002.name: Remote Services: SMB/Windows Admin Shares
T1021.002.description: Adversaries may use SMB and admin shares to move between systems.

T1021.006.name: Remote Services: Windows Remote Management
T1021.006.description: Adversaries may use WinRM to interact with and run commands on remote systems.

T1027.name: Obfuscated Files or Information
T1027.description: Adversaries may obfuscate content to make detection or analysis harder.

T1046.name: Network Service Discovery
T1046.description: Adversaries may scan hosts for open ports and running services.

T1053.005.name: Scheduled Task/Job: Scheduled Task
T1053.005.description: Adversaries may abuse task scheduling to run code at a set time or at startup.

T1059.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
T1059.description: Adversaries may abuse command and script interpreters to execute commands.

T1059.001.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell
T1059.001.description: Adversaries may abuse PowerShell to execute commands and scripts.

T1070.001.name: Indicator Removal: Clear Windows Event Logs
T1070.001.description: Adversaries may clear Windows event logs to hide evidence of intrusion.

T1071.001.name: Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols
T1071.001.description: Adversaries may hide command-and-control traffic inside web protocol traffic.

T1105.name: Ingress Tool Transfer
T1105.description: Adversaries may transfer tools or files from an external system into the environment.

T1110.name: Brute Force
T1110.description: Adversaries may guess passwords repeatedly when credentials are unknown.

T1110.003.name: Brute Force: Password Spraying
T1110.003.description: Adversaries may try one or a few common passwords against many accounts.

T1136.001.name: Create Account: Local Account
T1136.001.description: Adversaries may create a local account to maintain access.

T1204.002.name: User Execution: Malicious File
T1204.002.description: Adversaries may rely on a user opening a malicious file to gain execution.

T1218.005.name: System Binary Proxy Execution: Mshta
T1218.005.description: Adversaries may abuse mshta.exe to proxy execution of malicious content.

T1218.010.name: System Binary Proxy Execution: Regsvr32
T1218.010.description: Adversaries may abuse regsvr32.exe to proxy execution of malicious code.

T1218.011.name: System Binary Proxy Execution: Rundll32
T1218.011.description: Adversaries may abuse rundll32.exe to proxy execution of malicious code.

T1490.name: Inhibit System Recovery
T1490.description: Adversaries may delete or disable recovery features such as shadow copies.

T1547.001.name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
T1547.001.description: Adversaries may add programs to Run keys or startup folders to run at logon.

T1571.name: Non-Standard Port
T1571.description: Adversaries may use a protocol on an unexpected port to avoid simple filtering.
